message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that shows **how** to pull *only* the `id` and `context` fields for the CAA record(s) belonging to `sample2.com`.  
I’ll give two common patterns – one for a typical JSON‑over‑REST API and another for a GraphQL‑style interface – so you can adapt it to whatever provider you’re working against.  

> ⚠️ Make sure your API key (`secret567`) has read access to DNS records before running anything.

---

## 1️⃣ REST API (query parameters)

Many providers expose a “list” endpoint where you can narrow down both the type of record and the columns returned.

```bash
curl \
    --request GET \
    --url   "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?record_type=CAA&fields=id,context" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer secret567"
```

### What this does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/v1/domains/sample2.com/records` | Target domain’s record list |
| `?record_type=CAA` | Filter to only CAA records |
| `&fields=id,context` | Tell the server to return *just* those two properties |

#### Expected Response (JSON)

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "rec_123456",
      "context": { "issue":"letsencrypt.org","iodef":"mailto:dns-admin@example.com"}
    },
    {
      "id": "rec_789012",
      "context": { "issuewild":"digicert.com" }
    }
  ],
  "meta": { "total_records": 2 }
}
```

Only the `id` and nested `context` objects appear—everything else is omitted.

---

## 2️⃣ GraphQL (field selection)

If your provider uses GraphQL, you can explicitly pick the fields you care about:

```graphql
query GetCaaRecords($domain:"String!") {
  dns(domain:$domain) {
    caaRecords {
      id
      context
    }
  }
}
```

Send it over HTTP POST:

```bash
curl \
    --request POST \
    --url   "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/graphql" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \
    --data '{"query":"query GetCaaRecords($domain:String!){dns(domain:$domain){caaRecords{id context}} }","variables":{"domain":"sample2.com"}}'
```

Result will look like:

```json
{
  "data":{
    "dns":{
      "caaRecords":[
        {"id":"rec_123456","context":{"issue":"letsencrypt.org"}},
        {"id":"rec_789012","context":{"issuewild":"digicert.com"}}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Again, only the requested fields surface.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick sanity check

After you run either request, verify that the payload contains **no other keys** besides `id`, `context`, and possibly wrapper metadata (`data`, `meta`). If you see extra fields, double‑check the documentation for your provider—it may require a different parameter name (`include_fields`, `projection`, etc.) or a slightly altered URL path.

---

## TL;DR

| Method | Endpoint | Key Query Params | Result |
|--------|----------|------------------|--------|
| REST | `/domains/{name}/records` | `record_type=CAA&fields=id,context` | Only ID + Context |
| GraphQL | `/graphql` | `{ id context }` inside query | Same result |

Replace `yourdnsprovider.com` with the actual host, keep `secret567` in the Authorization header, and you’re good to go!
